people.label: Alexandro C. Wiggins
people.sub: Senior Chief Petty Officer (Operations Specialist), US Navy; USS Jackson (LCS-6) witness
people.narrative: Alexandro C. Wiggins is a US Navy Senior Chief Petty Officer, an Operations Specialist with roughly twenty-three years of service, who testified in uniform and on active duty before the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets on 9 September 2025. That fact alone distinguishes him from almost every witness who preceded him: Fravor, Graves, Grusch and Elizondo all testified after leaving service. Wiggins's written statement places him aboard USS Jackson (LCS-6) on 15 February 2023 at approximately 1915 PST in the W-291 Warning Area off Southern California. He states he 'visually observed a light rising from the waterline, consistent with a platform emerging from the ocean rather than distant surface lights or celestial rise.' The object was self-luminous and Tic Tac-shaped; it joined three similar objects; the four held controlled geometry and departed simultaneously with near-instantaneous acceleration, producing no sonic boom, no exhaust plume and displaying no visible control surfaces - characteristics he described as inconsistent with conventional aircraft or drones. Combat Information Center personnel recorded the event on the ship's Star SAFIRE multi-spectral EO/IR system and reported to the Tactical Action Officer. The footage was subsequently published by journalists Jeremy Corbell and George Knapp. Wiggins is therefore a rare complete chain: a named, credentialed, serving witness; a specified date, time and operating area; a named sensor system; a documented internal report; and released imagery.

entities.desc: The statutory destination for federal UAP records, established by the National Archives under sections 1841-1843 of the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act. The statute requires NARA to establish the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection and requires each federal agency to review, identify and organise each UAP record, defined to include copies of all Government, Government-provided or Government-funded records relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena, technologies of unknown origin, and non-human intelligence. NARA's guidance directed agencies holding releasable UAP records to contact it to initiate transfers before 30 September 2025, in digital form with proper metadata. As of 12 August 2026, seven agencies appear as contributors in RG 615: the Federal Aviation Administration, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the National Security Agency, the Department of State and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The absences are the story. There is no CIA series. No Defense Intelligence Agency series. No Department of Energy, no NASA, no National Reconnaissance Office, no National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, no Department of Homeland Security, and no separate Army, Navy or Air Force series - the services appear, if at all, inside OSD. Nor is there any contractor material, because no statute reaches contractor holdings. NARA publishes no compliance list, no roster of agencies determined to hold covered records, and no statement identifying non-compliant agencies; its FAQ describes the framework and is silent on implementation status. The volumetric picture in the bulk-download inventory as last updated 24 April 2025 is equally telling: the electronic-records contributions are tiny - NRC 11.74MB, ODNI 1.29MB, FAA 63.10MB, OSD 103.37MB - against tens of terabytes of legacy Project BLUE BOOK and Roswell material, including a sanitized Blue Book case-file series of roughly 379GB split across ten files and 36.48GB of BLUE BOOK still pictures. entities.label: ODNI Memorandum ES 2026-00818 - Preliminary Guidance for Implementation of NDA Waiver
entities.sub: Signed by Aaron Lukas, Principal Deputy DNI; released by Rep. Burlison 1 August 2026
entities.desc: The single most important primary document of the current cycle, and the first paper instrument to name PURSUE as an entity rather than a website. An unclassified ODNI memorandum, control number ES 2026-00818, headed MEMORANDUM FOR DISTRIBUTION and signed by Aaron Lukas, Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, subject 'Preliminary Guidance for Implementation of NDA Waiver'. Rep. Eric Burlison obtained it and published it on 1 August 2026. Its opening sentence establishes the architecture: the memorandum 'provides preliminary guidance for the release of all Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) information to the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE) Task Force for review and declassification.' PURSUE is therefore a task force with a declassification review function, not merely a publication portal - and it is a task force to which 'all' UAP information across the Intelligence Community is to be released. The operative direction: consistent with Presidential Direction, the Department of War and the Intelligence Community will implement a process ensuring that current and former government employees and contractors with relevant UAP information 'shall have prior non-disclosure agreements (NDA), agreements, oaths, or commitments waived when speaking with authorized government representatives of the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) or PURSUE.' The word 'oaths' is doing heavy work: it reaches beyond signed NDAs to the oral secrecy commitments characteristic of unacknowledged special access programmes. All IC members are directed, within 30 days of receipt, to coordinate with ODNI to establish a PURSUE designee and to inform their workforce of the President's order; to ensure the workforce knows that 'any previous or existing NDAs prohibiting disclosure to the President, or designees like PURSUE, are no longer in force'; and that anyone with knowledge of UAP information 'should report all such information to AARO, or to an authorized PURSUE representative.' Detailed reporting procedures were to be disseminated to IC components within a further 30 days, and DoW and ODNI were to issue departments and agencies detailed implementation guidance 'for the broader PURSUE transparency project.' The distribution list is the IC in full: the Directors of CIA, DIA, NGA, NRO, NSA and FBI; the Under Secretary for Intelligence and Security, Department of War; the Under Secretary for Intelligence and Analysis, DHS; the Assistant Secretary for Intelligence and Research, State; the Assistant Secretary for Intelligence and Analysis, Treasury; the Chief of Intelligence, DEA; the Director of the Office of Intelligence and Counterintelligence, Department of Energy; the Deputy Chief of Staff for Intelligence, US Army; the Director of Intelligence, US Marine Corps; the Director of Naval Intelligence; the Deputy Chief of Staff for Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance, US Air Force; the Deputy Chief of Space Operations for Intelligence, US Space Force; and the Assistant Commandant for Intelligence, US Coast Guard. Read against Record Group 615, the list is an indictment: CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA, DOE and the military departments are all addressees of an ODNI memorandum on UAP information and none of them has a series in the statutory National Archives UAP collection.

entities.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA
entities.sub: Adopted by the House 22-23 July 2026; pending in the Senate
entities.desc: The successor to the 2023 Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act, and the first time such a framework has cleared a chamber. Adopted by the House on 22 July 2026 as an amendment to the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act - the first year Burlison's UAP disclosure amendment advanced to a House floor vote, after a similar proposal failed to advance in the previous defence-bill cycle. As adopted it establishes a statutory framework for preserving, reviewing and publicly disclosing UAP records; creates a permanent UAP Records Collection at the National Archives; establishes an independent, Senate-confirmed UAP Records Review Board with subpoena authority to determine what is released and what stays classified; requires federal agencies to identify, organise, preserve and transmit UAP records to the National Archives on a statutory timeline; and - the provision with no precedent in existing authority - extends disclosure requirements to covered government contractors. Burlison's own framing places it in support of the executive programme rather than against it: the press release states the amendment supports President Trump's Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters. Read structurally, it is the exact remedy for each defect PURSUE has: PURSUE has no statutory timeline, so the amendment supplies one; PURSUE has no subpoena power, so the amendment creates a board that has one; PURSUE cannot reach Lockheed, Battelle or MITRE, so the amendment extends to contractors; PURSUE's decisions are made by an unchartered task force, so the amendment's board is Senate-confirmed. It is not law. It must survive the Senate's own version and conference later in 2026 and be signed. The 2023 precedent is the reason for pessimism: the original UAP Disclosure Act's eminent-domain and review-board provisions were stripped in conference by House Intelligence and Armed Services leadership before the FY2024 NDAA was signed.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 01 posted at war.gov/UFO
timeline.text: The first PURSUE tranche: a 1.2GB document bundle and a 1.3GB video bundle, 160 files spanning 1944 to 2026, published at war.gov/UFO with no manifest, no metadata and no assessment.

timeline.label: DefenseScoop reports the programme's name: PURSUE
timeline.text: DefenseScoop publishes the acronym - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters - and the research community's reaction. Christopher Mellon: 'Data alone is not disclosure.' Ryan Graves: 'Ambiguous imagery without that surrounding data is hard for pilots, researchers, or the public to evaluate responsibly.'

timeline.label: UAP Science Advisory Council announced under Avi Loeb
timeline.text: Avi Loeb announces a twelve-plus-member scientific advisory council reporting to the UAP Governance Board, five weeks into a release programme that assesses nothing it publishes.

timeline.label: AARO sponsors an unannounced UAP research workshop
timeline.text: Roughly 40 government, academic and independent researchers meet in the Washington DC area, hosted by Associated Universities, Inc., to standardise UAP data capture and analysis. No attendee list is published; the event is not reported publicly until March 2026.

timeline.label: House Oversight Task Force hears five UAP witnesses
timeline.text: Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp, Borland and Spielberger testify in HVC-210. Rep. Burlison plays previously unseen video of an MQ-9 firing a Hellfire missile at a high-speed orb off Yemen in October 2024; the object appears struck and not destroyed.

timeline.label: NARA transfer deadline for UAP records passes
timeline.text: NARA's guidance directed agencies holding releasable UAP records to initiate transfers before 30 September 2025. As of 12 August 2026 seven agencies appear in RG 615 - FAA, NRC, ODNI, OSD, NSA, State and FBI - and NARA has published no compliance list and no statement about agencies that did not transfer.

timeline.label: FY2026 NDAA carries three UAP provisions
timeline.text: The conferenced bill requires AARO to brief Congress on NORAD/NORTHCOM UAP intercepts since 2004 including data collected, to account for UAP-related security classification guides, and to streamline agency data-sharing.

timeline.label: Burlison demands MITRE's UAP records back to 1930
timeline.text: A ten-page letter with over 40 production requests, a 45-day deadline, native electronic format with complete metadata, naming eleven other contractors in scope. MITRE says it will coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work.

timeline.label: Navy reports ~100 UAP and two uncrewed surface systems off Virginia
timeline.text: Disclosed the same day AARO's FY2025 annual report appeared; the sole maritime case in that report; no case number, date, hull or unit made public.

timeline.label: Task Force holds MKULTRA hearing
timeline.text: 'Mind Control and Accountability: Uncovering the Truth of the CIA's MKULTRA Project' - the same declassification task force that carries the UAP file turns to CIA behavioural programmes, establishing that its remit is agency secrecy generally.

timeline.label: Trump directs release of UAP files by Truth Social post
timeline.text: The originating instrument of PURSUE: a social-media direction to Secretary of War Hegseth and other departments to begin identifying and releasing government files on alien and extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs. No signed executive order has surfaced.

timeline.label: Hegseth commits the Department: 'full compliance with that executive order'
timeline.text: At an Arsenal of Freedom stop in Louisville, Colorado, the Secretary of War describes a deliberative process and declines a timeline. Sue Gough confirms AARO's caseload has passed 2,000, with about 1,000 reports in an Active Archive for insufficient data.

timeline.label: White House registers alien.gov and aliens.gov
timeline.text: Neither domain is connected to a site. Anna Kelly: 'Stay tuned!' The release programme ships seven weeks later on war.gov/UFO instead.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 02: 51 sensor videos and ODNI-UAP-D001
timeline.text: A 5.6GB video bundle, the largest of the five, plus the first-person narrative of a serving senior intelligence officer describing a one-hour multi-witness encounter from a military helicopter in late 2025.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 03: 72 files, FBI the largest contributor
timeline.text: 53 documents, 10 images, 6 videos, 3 audio files; 29 FBI files including agents' own first-hand orb observations; a less-redacted CIA Robertson Panel report; documents 826MB, video 4.6GB.

timeline.label: Grusch speaks on the Capitol steps at a Luna press conference
timeline.text: David Grusch tells reporters the government is aware of 'several' kinds of alien life, describing 'a continuum from corporeal bipedal type life to what I would consider as sentient plasmoid life,' and references four different species. It is his most specific public claim about biology.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 04: no file count published
timeline.text: 227MB of documents and 1.4GB of video, content dating to the 1940s. The Department publishes no file count - by the fourth tranche the release programme had stopped stating what it was releasing.

timeline.label: Burlison demands CIA and FBI records on Varginha 1996
timeline.text: The congressional records demand crosses a border for the first time, aimed at the two agencies whose positions on the UAP record are most conspicuous.

timeline.label: AARO publishes the FY2025 annual report, months late
timeline.text: 319 new reports, 370 resolutions all to conventional causes, 50 UAS notifications near nuclear infrastructure against 18 the year before, and 255 of 262 secure-channel submissions assessed out of scope.

timeline.label: House adopts the UAP Disclosure Act as an FY2027 NDAA amendment
timeline.text: A permanent National Archives collection, a Senate-confirmed Records Review Board with subpoena power, statutory transfer timelines, and disclosure obligations extended to covered government contractors. First time such a framework has cleared a chamber.

timeline.label: Burlison publicises the Presidential UAP NDA-waiver directive
timeline.text: He offers his office's assistance to witnesses, warns that it is unclear whether the abrogation covers testimony given to Congress before referral to the executive branch, and recommends witnesses bring both an attorney and a member of Congress.

timeline.label: ODNI memorandum ES 2026-00818 published: PURSUE is a Task Force
timeline.text: Aaron Lukas, Principal Deputy DNI, directs release of all IC UAP information to the PURSUE Task Force for review and declassification, waives NDAs, agreements, oaths and commitments for those speaking to AARO or PURSUE, and requires every IC element to name a PURSUE designee within 30 days.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 05: the Gulf of Oman gunship engagement
timeline.text: 41 files - 16 videos, 22 documents, 3 images - including six AC-130J videos and DOW-UAP-D101 on the 8 September 2021 Gulf of Oman encounter, and the 1953 Navy Photographic Interpretation Center analysis of the Great Falls and Tremonton films.

timeline.label: The Black Vault publishes a searchable mirror of Release 01
timeline.text: Three days after the first tranche, John Greenewald strips password protection from the released PDFs, runs OCR, generates transcripts and subtitles and adds agency categorisation - supplying the index the government did not.

timeline.label: DoW OIG withholds its UAP evaluation methodology under (b)(1)
timeline.text: Fourth interim release in DODIG-2021-000806: the 'Potential Benefits' section withheld on national-security grounds, background sections marked (S//NF) blacked out, methodology steps 3-8 redacted, October 2020 UAP Task Force leadership meeting withheld as deliberative. Approximately 245 pages still pending.

timeline.label: Sol Foundation publishes peer-reviewed analysis of possible UAP material
timeline.text: Science and Policy Briefing No. 3 by Marik von Rennenkampff reports atomic and isotopic analysis of physical material associated with a multi-witness event, conducted by Garry Nolan - the private-sector counterpart to AARO's two Oak Ridge specimen studies.

timeline.label: Sol Foundation confirms its co-founders sit on the federal advisory council
timeline.text: Nolan and Skafish are named to the UAP Science Advisory Council, which the foundation says was announced by ODNI with FBI support and reports to an interagency UAP Governance Board. All data shared with the council will be unclassified.

timeline.label: AARO solicits a JWICS-hosted case management system
timeline.text: Its first market research solicitation, three years after standing up: a custom case system on the Top Secret/SCI intranet to track UAP data, interactions and records and to support a planned public reporting mechanism. Capability statements due 9 June 2025.

timeline.label: Elizondo's claimed 600-1,000-foot disc identified as an irrigation circle
timeline.text: At a UAP Disclosure Fund hearing Luis Elizondo presents an image described as a gigantic disc; analysts including Mick West identify it as an irrigation circle. The correction comes from the sceptic community, not the government.

timeline.label: 3I/ATLAS: an anomalous object and a furloughed government
timeline.text: The US government fields questions about the third known interstellar object during a shutdown, with no standing scientific body chartered to answer.

timeline.label: AARO's workshop white paper recommends metadata standards
timeline.text: Standardised metadata templates, AI with human oversight and open narrative reporting - published three months before a release programme that adopted none of them.

timeline.label: The Department of War publicly takes the file
timeline.text: Hegseth: 'We've got our people working on it right now... We're going to be in full compliance with [the president's request].' Asked about extraterrestrial life: 'We'll see. I get to do the review and find out along with you.' Press Secretary Kingsley Wilson says AARO is coordinating with the White House and across agencies to consolidate existing records.

timeline.label: The research community's first asks
timeline.text: Mellon: the impact depends on the follow-through. Gallaudet: 'I'll believe it when I see it.' Loeb: 'One step that can be taken immediately is to declassify events from 50 years ago.' Parnell: the department looks forward to working with the interagency.

timeline.label: MITRE's 45-day production deadline falls
timeline.text: No public production has been reported as of 12 August 2026 in response to Burlison's 22 May demand for records back to 1930.

timeline.label: The council's ceiling is set on day one
timeline.text: All data shared with the UAP Science Advisory Council will be unclassified - a scientific advisory body without access to the classified holdings whose existence is the entire question.

timeline.label: EOP-UAP-D001: the Executive Office of the President becomes an originator
timeline.text: Release 05 carries a November 1963 Brazil incident report prefixed EOP, alongside DOS-UAP-D002, a State Department cable on the same events - the release programme reaching into White House holdings.

timeline.label: Parnell: additional files 'on a rolling basis'
timeline.text: The Department's only statement of forward intent: the material continues to be housed on WAR.GOV/UFO and more will follow. No schedule, no scope, no manifest.

timeline.label: Historical Record Report Volume II remains unpublished
timeline.text: Promised within months in November 2024, said in June 2025 to carry the Yankee Blue findings and scheduled for late 2025, and absent from AARO's Congressional and Press Products page on 12 August 2026 - after five PURSUE tranches and an IC-wide NDA waiver.

timeline.label: Five agencies ordered to release UAP information have no series in the statutory archive
timeline.text: CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA and DOE are addressees of ODNI ES 2026-00818 and absentees from Record Group 615. NARA publishes no compliance list and no statement identifying non-compliant agencies.

timeline.label: Vandenberg incursions during NRO launches (2003-2005)
timeline.text: Jeffrey Nuccetelli's testimony describes objects 'like flying buildings' over a space launch range during National Reconnaissance Office missions, each incident witnessed by multiple personnel, documented, investigated and reported up the chain. No Air Force series exists in RG 615 to hold those reports.

timeline.label: USS Jackson: a light rising from the waterline
timeline.text: At about 1915 PST in W-291 off Southern California, Senior Chief Alexandro Wiggins observes a self-luminous object emerge from the ocean, join three others, and depart with near-instantaneous acceleration. CIC records it on the ship's Star SAFIRE and reports to the Tactical Action Officer.

timeline.label: An MQ-9 fires a Hellfire missile at an orb off Yemen
timeline.text: The object appears struck and is not destroyed. The video is not shown publicly until Rep. Burlison plays it at a hearing eleven months later; the Department has never confirmed it.

timeline.label: The Senate's FY2027 base text contains no UAP provisions
timeline.text: S. 4784 as reported (S. Rept. 119-127) returns zero occurrences of 'unidentified', 'UAP' or 'Anomaly Resolution'. The House-adopted disclosure framework must survive conference against a chamber that did not legislate on the subject at all.

entityInfo.title: The current cycle: PURSUE, the 2025-2026 hearings, and the machinery of release
entityInfo.scope: January 2025 to 12 August 2026. The PURSUE release programme in full - every tranche, its bundle URLs, its file identifiers and its critics; the September 2025 House Oversight Task Force hearing and its five witnesses; the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets; AARO under Kosloski, its FY2025 annual report, its JWICS case-management procurement, its unannounced Associated Universities workshop and the Historical Record Report Volume II it has still not published; National Archives Record Group 615 and the agencies that have and have not transferred; the ODNI NDA-waiver memorandum ES 2026-00818; the FY2026 NDAA UAP provisions and the House-adopted UAP Disclosure Act amendment to the FY2027 NDAA; the UAP Science Advisory Council and the UAP Governance Board; and the status of the wave-1 principals.
entityInfo.thesis: The 2026 disclosure episode is real, it is executive, and it is structurally incapable of answering the question the board exists to ask. A Truth Social post produced a task force with declassification authority over the entire Intelligence Community, an IC-wide waiver of nondisclosure agreements, oaths and commitments, and roughly sixteen gigabytes of released material - all without a published executive order, a defined scope, a manifest, a metadata schema, or a single FOIA case number. In the same period the Department withheld its own UAP evaluation methodology under national-security exemption, the statutory National Archives collection received about 180MB of modern electronic records from seven agencies while CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA, DOE and the military departments transferred nothing, and the report that was supposed to resolve the reverse-engineering allegations - Historical Record Report Volume II - remained unpublished for the second consecutive year. Imagery flows; methodology, custody and provenance do not. The one instrument that would change that, the Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA, cleared the House on 22 July 2026 and faces a Senate base text with no UAP provisions in it at all.
entityInfo.methodNote: Every claim in this file is anchored to a URL fetched on or before 12 August 2026. The ODNI memorandum was retrieved as a PDF from burlison.house.gov and optically character-recognised locally because the released copy contains no machine-readable text; its quoted language is transcribed from that OCR and is marked tier 1. Where two sources disagree - the legal character of the UAP Science Advisory Council, or the date span of Release 05 - both accounts are recorded and the disagreement is stated rather than resolved.

gaps: No published charter, executive order, membership roster, chair, staff, budget line or physical location for the PURSUE Task Force, a body ODNI ES 2026-00818 credits with declassification authority over the Intelligence Community's entire UAP holdings.

No signed executive order on UAP declassification exists in the public record, despite Secretary Hegseth referring on 23 February 2026 to 'that executive order'. Whether an unpublished order exists is the single most answerable open question in the domain.
The signature date on ODNI ES 2026-00818 is not legible in the released copy, so the 30-day clocks it sets for IC PURSUE designees and for detailed reporting procedures cannot be timed.

No manifest, index, metadata schema or provenance statement has been published for any of the five PURSUE tranches; the file counts on this board come from Disclosure Archives, EarthSky and The Black Vault, not from the releasing authority.
Why many PURSUE PDFs were password-protected against optical character recognition is unexplained - a deliberate processing decision and an export artefact are both consistent with the evidence.

NARA publishes no compliance list for Record Group 615 and no statement identifying agencies determined to hold covered UAP records that have not transferred them. Whether CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA, DOE, NASA, DHS and the military departments made negative determinations or simply did not respond is unknown.

The bulk-download inventory for RG 615 was last updated 24 April 2025, before the 30 September 2025 transfer deadline and before the NSA, State and FBI catalog entries appeared; the current volumetric picture cannot be stated precisely.
AARO Historical Record Report Volume II: no publication date, no draft, no explanation, and no statement from Kosloski since the November 2024 commitment.
Rep. Luna's April 2026 letter, which PURSUE Release 02 is reported to answer, has not been published.
Whether MITRE produced anything responsive to Burlison's 22 May 2026 demand by the 45-day deadline that fell in early July 2026, and whether the eleven named contractors were separately approached.
No public response from CIA or FBI to Burlison's 8 July 2026 Varginha letters.
The UAP Governance Board has no published charter, roster or meeting record; its relationship to the PURSUE Task Force is undocumented.

Whether the UAP Science Advisory Council holds a Federal Advisory Committee Act charter and which agency sponsors it: DefenseScoop reports Avi Loeb formed and leads it, the Sol Foundation says ODNI announced it with FBI support.
No case number, incident date, hull or unit has been made public for the Navy report of approximately 100 airborne UAP and two uncrewed surface systems off the Virginia coast.

The provenance, unit, chain of custody and declassification authority of the October 2024 MQ-9 Yemen Hellfire video Rep. Burlison played on 9 September 2025 are unstated, and the Department has never confirmed it.

Whether the NORAD/NORTHCOM UAP intercept briefing required by the FY2026 NDAA - number, location, nature and data collected since 2004 - has been delivered to Congress, and whether any part of it will be made public.

AARO's accounting of UAP-related security classification guides, required by the FY2026 NDAA, has not surfaced. Those guides are the instruments that determine what may be said about a sighting before any declassification question arises.
The identity of the multi-witness event whose material was analysed in Sol Foundation Briefing No. 3, the specimen's chain of custody, and the journal of peer-reviewed publication.
Whether Sean Kirkpatrick's portfolio as ORNL chief technology officer for defense and intelligence programs encompasses the laboratory's AARO specimen analyses.

Whether the FY2027 NDAA conference will retain the House-adopted UAP Disclosure Act against a Senate base text (S. 4784) containing no UAP provisions - the direct test of whether 2026 produced law or only files.
No serving executive-branch official - not Kosloski, not the PURSUE Task Force chair, not the Principal Deputy DNI - has testified under oath on UAP in the 119th Congress.
_keyFindings: PURSUE is a Task Force, not a website: ODNI memorandum ES 2026-00818, signed by Principal Deputy DNI Aaron Lukas and published by Rep. Burlison on 1 August 2026, directs the release of all Intelligence Community UAP information to the 'PURSUE Task Force for review and declassification'. No charter, roster, chair or executive order for that body is public.

The NDA waiver reaches unwritten obligations. ES 2026-00818 waives 'non-disclosure agreements (NDA), agreements, oaths, or commitments' for those speaking to AARO or PURSUE - language only load-bearing if oral secrecy commitments exist.

The memorandum's distribution list and Record Group 615's contributor list are mirror images. CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA, DOE and every military department are addressees of the release directive and absentees from the statutory archive.

The government published no manifest for any tranche. war.gov/UFO lists only date and bundle sizes; every per-tranche file count in circulation comes from third parties. Many released PDFs were password-protected against OCR, and the operative public index is John Greenewald's private mirror.

Imagery is releasable; methodology is not. In June 2026 the DoW OIG withheld the 'Potential Benefits' section of its own UAP evaluation proposal under exemption (b)(1) and fully redacted methodology steps three through eight, with about 245 pages still pending in DODIG-2021-000806.

The record now contains multiple US weapons engagements of unidentified objects that were not destroyed: the October 2024 MQ-9 Hellfire shot off Yemen shown by Rep. Burlison, DOW-UAP-PR051's MQ-9 weapons-quality lock, and the 8 September 2021 AC-130J encounter in the Gulf of Oman with DOW-UAP-D101. No AARO annual report characterises any of them as an engagement.
EOP-UAP-D001 in Release 05 establishes the Executive Office of the President as an originating authority in the UAP records universe, on a November 1963 Brazil incident.

AARO's own convened experts told it what to do and the release programme did the opposite: the February 2026 workshop white paper recommended standardised metadata templates, AI with human oversight and open narrative reporting; the tranches from May 2026 carried none of the three.
AARO had no purpose-built case management system until it solicited one in May 2025, to be hosted on JWICS - meaning the consolidated UAP case record now lives at Top Secret/SCI by default.
Historical Record Report Volume II is still unpublished on 12 August 2026, after five tranches, an IC-wide NDA waiver and a late FY2025 annual report.
